notes.summary: This chapter deals with the area and perimeter of a circle and its parts: arcs, sectors and segments. CBSE tests it through 1-mark MCQs and assertion-reason items on the formulas, and 2-3 mark real-life problems such as clock hands, car wipers, grazing animals, umbrellas and lighthouses.
keyPoints: Circle of radius r: circumference = 2πr, area = πr². Example: r = 7 cm gives 44 cm and 154 cm² (π = 22/7).
Length of the arc of a sector of angle θ: l = (θ/360) × 2πr. Example: r = 21 cm, θ = 60° gives l = 22 cm.
Area of a sector = (θ/360) × πr² = ½ × l × r. Example: r = 21 cm, θ = 60° gives 231 cm².
Perimeter of a sector = arc length + 2r; perimeter of a semicircle = πr + 2r (not just πr).
Area of minor segment = area of sector − area of the triangle formed by the two radii. For θ = 90° the triangle is ½r²; for θ = 60° it is equilateral with area (√3/4)r².
Major sector = πr² − minor sector; major segment = πr² − minor segment.
Clock hands: the minute hand turns 6° per minute (5 minutes = 30°, 30 minutes = 180°); the hour hand turns 30° per hour.
If the radius is multiplied by k, the circumference becomes k times and the area becomes k² times (radius doubled → area 4 times).
Grazing problems: a rope of length r tied at a corner of a rectangular field lets the animal graze a quadrant of area ¼πr².
As per the CBSE syllabus, segment-area problems are restricted to central angles of 60° and 90°.
traps: Using the diameter in place of the radius; always halve the diameter first.
Forgetting to add 2r while finding the perimeter of a sector or a semicircle.
Converting time to angle wrongly: 5 minutes of the minute hand is 30°, not 5°.
Giving the major segment when the minor segment is asked (or vice versa), or subtracting the wrong triangle area.
Mixing π = 22/7 and π = 3.14; use the value stated in the question or the answer will not match the options.
notes.examTip: Reduce θ/360 to a simple fraction first (60° → 1/6, 90° → 1/4, 120° → 1/3) and cancel it with r² before multiplying; this saves time and avoids arithmetic slips.

questions.text: The minute hand of a clock is 14 cm long. Find the area swept by the minute hand in 5 minutes. (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation:
The minute hand turns 360° in 60 minutes, i.e. 6° per minute, so in 5 minutes it turns 30°.
Area swept = (θ/360) × πr² = (30/360) × (22/7) × 14 × 14.
= (1/12) × 616 = 154/3 cm² ≈ 51.33 cm².
(22/3 is the arc length in cm, and 308/3 would be the area for 60°.)

questions.text: Find the length of the arc of a sector of angle 45° in a circle of radius 28 cm. (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation:
Arc length l = (θ/360) × 2πr.
l = (45/360) × 2 × (22/7) × 28 = (1/8) × 176.
l = 22 cm.
(308 is the area of the sector in cm², and 11 cm comes from wrongly using πr instead of 2πr.)

questions.text: If the circumference and the area of a circle are numerically equal, the radius of the circle is
questions.explanation:
Circumference = area gives 2πr = πr².
Dividing both sides by πr (r ≠ 0): r = 2.
So the radius is 2 units (4 units is the diameter).

questions.text: A chord of a circle of radius 10 cm subtends a right angle at the centre. Find the area of the minor segment. (Use π = 3.14)
questions.explanation:
Area of the sector = (90/360) × 3.14 × 10² = ¼ × 314 = 78.5 cm².
The two radii and the chord form a right triangle of area ½ × 10 × 10 = 50 cm².
Area of minor segment = sector − triangle = 78.5 − 50 = 28.5 cm².
(285.5 cm² is the major segment: 314 − 28.5.)

questions.text: A car has a single wiper on its rear windscreen. The wiper blade is 21 cm long and sweeps through an angle of 120°. Find the area cleaned in one sweep of the blade. (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation:
The blade sweeps a sector of radius 21 cm and angle 120°.
Area = (120/360) × (22/7) × 21 × 21 = (1/3) × 1386.
Area = 462 cm².
(44 is the arc length in cm and 1386 cm² is the full circle.)

questions.text: A lighthouse spreads a red warning light over a sector of angle 72° up to a distance of 10 km. Find the area of the sea over which ships are warned. (Use π = 3.14)
questions.explanation:
The warned region is a sector of radius 10 km and angle 72°.
Area = (72/360) × 3.14 × 10² = (1/5) × 314.
Area = 62.8 km².
(12.56 km is the arc length and 314 km² is the full circle.)

questions.text: The arc of a sector of a circle of radius 21 cm has length 22 cm. Find the area of the sector. (Use π = 22/7)

Assertion (A): The area of a sector of angle 90° in a circle of radius 14 cm is 77 cm². (Use π = 22/7)
Reason (R): A sector of angle 90° (a quadrant) has one-fourth the area of the whole circle.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.explanation:
R is true because 90/360 = 1/4.
Area of the circle = (22/7) × 14 × 14 = 616 cm², so the quadrant = 616 ÷ 4 = 154 cm², not 77 cm².
Hence A is false and R is true.

questions.text:
Assertion (A): The perimeter of a sector of radius r and central angle θ is (θ/360) × 2πr + 2r.
Reason (R): The perimeter of a semicircle of radius r is πr.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.explanation:
A sector is bounded by one arc and two radii, so its perimeter = arc length + 2r = (θ/360) × 2πr + 2r. A is true.
A semicircle is a sector of angle 180°, so its perimeter = πr + 2r; πr is only the curved part. R is false.
Hence A is true but R is false.

questions.text: A chord of a circle of radius 14 cm subtends an angle of 90° at the centre. Find the area of the major segment of the circle. (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation:
Area of circle = (22/7) × 14 × 14 = 616 cm².
Minor sector = ¼ × 616 = 154 cm²; triangle formed by the radii = ½ × 14 × 14 = 98 cm².
Minor segment = 154 − 98 = 56 cm².
Major segment = 616 − 56 = 560 cm².
(462 cm² is the major sector, not the major segment.)

questions.text: Two arcs of two different circles have equal lengths. If the arcs subtend angles of 60° and 75° at the centres of their respective circles, the ratio of the radii of the two circles is
questions.explanation:
Arc length = (θ/360) × 2πr.
Equal arcs: (60/360) × 2πr₁ = (75/360) × 2πr₂, so 60 r₁ = 75 r₂.
r₁/r₂ = 75/60 = 5/4.
So r₁ : r₂ = 5 : 4 (the arc with the smaller angle belongs to the larger circle).
